::api-operation{method="DELETE" path="/v1/businesses/{biz}/subscriptions/{sub}"}
#docs
Removes the subscription from the account. Allowed in any status, and it is NOT a cancellation: no cancellation is recorded, no final invoice is raised and no credit is issued, so deleting an active subscription simply stops billing it. To close the term out properly, cancel it instead. Everything it produced is kept and stays on the customer — invoices, payments and their ledger entries — and an unpaid invoice remains payable and stays in dunning. Reads of a deleted subscription return 404 and it no longer appears in lists.

## Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `biz` | `string` | **yes** | Business id (biz_…) |
| `sub` | `string` | **yes** | Subscription id (sub_…) |

## Headers

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | `string` | no | Safely retry writes — repeats return the original response. If a write FAILED after it had already taken effect, that failure is what repeats: the key is spent, and a new attempt needs a new key. |

## Response

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `object` | `string` | The object type; always `subscription`. One of `subscription`. |
| `id` | `string` | The subscription id. |
| `deleted` | `boolean` | Always true. |

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Deleted |
| `404` | No such subscription |
| `409` | Idempotency-Key conflict — the key is already in flight, or was reused with a different request payload. |

#request
```bash [Request]
curl -X DELETE "$TMBILLING_URL/v1/businesses/biz_XXXXXXXXXXXX01/subscriptions/sub_XXXXXXXXXXXX01" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TMBILLING_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)"
```

}
